This appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of award dated 07.02.2014 passed by 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Seoni in Claim Case No. 135/2011 seeking exoneration from liability to pay the compensation/setting aside of impugned award and respondents No. 1 to 5/applicant

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: have filed cross objections for enhancement of the compensation.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company submits that at the time of incident,
deceased was travelling in pickup vehicle as gratuitous passenger.
No premium has been paid with respect to deceased.

Further, after referring and relying on MA No. 602/2013 (Shriram Gendral Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Habib Khan and others), decided on 24.02.2025, it is urged that, in the instant case, principle of pay and recover cannot be applied.

sentences.text: Further, no enhancement is required in the compensation and cross objections filed by the respondents No. 1 to 5 be dismissed.

3. Learned counsel for the respondents No. 1 to 5/applicants submits that deceased used to trade in mangoes and at the time of accident, deceased was travelling in the cabin of pickup vehicle along with mangoes.
Therefore, learned tribunal has rightly fastened liability on insurance company to pay the compensation.
During submissions of learned counsel for the appellant submits that he does not wish to press cross objections, filed on behalf of the respondent No.1 to 5/claimant.
On above grounds, it is urged that appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

ANALYSIS AND FINDINGS:-.
5.

Having regard to nature of controversy involved in the case, the sole issue before this Court is whether at the time of accident, deceased was travelling in the cabin of offending vehicle as owner of the goods.
In claim petition, it has been mentioned that at the time of accident, deceased was going from Khurai to Nagpur to sale sacks of mangoes and he was traveling in the vehicle to look after the same.

Applicant witnesses Smt.Reshma Begam and Ishwar Lade have deposed in their examination-in-chief that at the time of accident, deceased was going to Nagpur for sale of sacks of mangoes along with two others and there were sacks of mangoes in the offending vehicle.

It is also mentioned in examination-in-chief of aforesaid applicant witnesses that at the time of accident,
deceased was traveling as owner of mangoes and to look after/for the safety of the aforesaid goods.
From testimonies of applicant witness Ishwar Lade, it appears that he was also going along with deceased in offending vehicle to sale his own sacks of mangoes.
6.
Now question arises as to whether on aforesaid point, applicant witnesses Smt.Rashma Begam and Ishwar Lade are reliable and trustworthy witnesses ?
7. With respect to aforesaid, facts mentioned in FIR, Spot Panchnama and Final Report are relevant.

10. Thus, from FIR (Ex.P/1A), Spot Punchnama (Ex.P/2A) and Final Report (Ex.P/6A) also,
testimony of applicant witnesses stands corroborated.
11. Hence, from evidence available on record, it is clearly established that at the relevant point of time, deceased was travelling in the cabin of offending vehicle as owner of the goods.
12. In the instant case, appellant/Insurance Company did not adduce any evidence to the effect that even owner of the goods, was not covered under the insurance policy and he was not insured.

It is also evident that insurance company did not adduce any evidence to the effect that at the time of accident, offending vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy.
There is nothing in the cross-examination of applicant witnesses so as to show that at the time of accident, offending was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy.
No such suggestion has been given to any of the applicant witnesses.

13. Hence, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, principle laid by Co- ordinate Bench of this Court Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd. (supra), does not help appellant in any manner whatsoever.

14. Resultantly, in view of discussion in foregoing paras, having regard to evidence available on record, in this Court's considered opinion, it is not established at all that at the time of accident,
offending vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy and it is also not established that tribunal has erred in fastening liability on appellant/Insurance Company for payment of compensation.
15.
Hence, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, in this Court's con- sidered opinion, no ground is made out for interfering in the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant/Insurance Company is liable to be dismissed.

17. Resultantly, appeal filed by the appellant/Insurance company and cross objections filed by respondents/claimants are dismissed and findings recorded by the Tribunal are affirmed as such.
18. Hence, this appeal filed by the appellant and cross objection filed by the respondents/claimants are disposed off accordingly.
